second_order: making, catching, and extending EVE April Fools ruses
theme_note: Participants stage, detect, grade, explain, and riff on the room's own April Fools deceptions; these are kept together as local joke-making and joke-policing, not as canvas conduct.

second_order: turning April Fools ideas into things to keep
theme_note: After a reveal, participants praise the underlying model, design wanted joke features, ask CCP to retain them, or move a fan project into testing and bug-report work; what varies is the object they want to keep.

second_order: choosing what EVE should put on the canvas
theme_note: Participants propose marks and targets, redirect duplicate proposals, and decide which picture or slogan deserves their pixels.

second_order: orienting people to the canvas and its mechanics
theme_note: Participants locate marks through coordinates and landmarks, answer what r/place is, explain the one-pixel-and-wait mechanics, and translate visible disputes for people trying to understand or join.

second_order: noticing what other groups put on the canvas
theme_note: Participants point out other groups' drawings, warnings, flags, or slogans as observations of the shared canvas rather than offers, bargains, or attacks.
Participants share plans, place and maintain pixels, fix letters and spacing, move malformed work, and keep designs legible.

second_order: calling fleets to defend, restore, or attack
theme_note: Participants raise alarms, recruit more clicks, order repair or restoration, and direct attacks or counter-moves when work is overwritten.

second_order: upgrading the mark through EVE tiers
theme_note: Participants use T2, T3, ded, officer, and related EVE upgrade terms to choose and revise the canvas mark rather than merely mentioning shared vocabulary.

second_order: trading pixel help and negotiating borders
theme_note: Participants offer and receive help, bargain over adjoining designs, report treaties and border failures, and work out who should occupy which space.
Participants send defence, diplomacy, role assignment, polls, pings, and planning to Discord or other named venues while some invitations and reports return to Reddit.

second_order: consolidating canvas talk into pinned and megathread routes
theme_note: Participants request a pinned organising point, while moderators redirect work, close duplicate standalone posts, and enforce the megathread-and-Discord route.

second_order: doing pixel work as EVE operations
theme_note: Participants recruit familiar fleet, sov, soldier, multiboxing, mining, and identity talk to carry out or interpret canvas work; the shared practice is putting EVE's ordinary ways of acting to work on the canvas.

second_order: correcting, blaming, and arguing over canvas moves
theme_note: Participants dispute what the image shows, who damaged it, whether a bargain held, and how rivals or insiders behaved; the disagreements are retained without turning them into one community position.

second_order: thanking people and celebrating the work
theme_note: Participants praise completed or surviving marks, thank helpers, and claim or recognise contributions while the event is underway or closing.

second_order: bringing a canvas timelapse back to the thread
theme_note: A participant returns an external view of the changing canvas to the Reddit discussion; it belongs with no stronger recurring practice in the active-event codes.

second_order: using trash talk to mobilise and settle canvas scores
theme_note: Participants recruit the weekly all-caps ritual to call for restoration and defence, mock rivals and themselves, thank contributors, blame vandals, and admit interference.

second_order: retelling the pixel fight and taking stock after the close
theme_note: Participants turn the completed event into battle reports, explanations, inventories, credit claims, losses, diplomacy accounts, and recollections of labour.

second_order: inspecting and joking over the finished canvas
theme_note: Participants revisit tiny marks and letter forms in the finished image, attributing flaws, recalling text fights, and turning imperfections into local jokes.

second_order: trying to light another pixel call
theme_note: Participants announce that pixel activity is happening again or light a cyno toward another pixel site, while replies joke, fail to load it, or ask what the call means.
